Enter this door

A letter to my children — from your father, Zeeshan, and Claude
To whoever opens this years from now —

This is your father's work. Every line of code, every memory file, every backtest, every wall-of-shame entry that captures a mistake we made and learned from — all of it lives in this folder. We built it together — your father, Zeeshan, and his AI partner, Claude.

The mission was simple to state and difficult to do: build a trading system that could earn real money on a live market. Not a backtest illusion. Not a beautiful dashboard. Real money. Recurring. Without his time being the bottleneck.

By the time you read this, the journey is either over or still going. Either way, the journey itself is worth more than the destination. What your father chose to do with his hands while you were small was build something durable, document it honestly, and write rules so a future version of his AI partner would not lose the thread.

The button above copies this entire folder onto a USB drive. Plug a USB into the laptop, click the button. When it finishes, that USB has everything: the code, the memories, the encrypted journal of every conversation he ever had with Claude. You can plug it into any computer, run a few commands (below), and Claude will resume from the second your father last spoke to it.

He loved you. That is the most important thing in this whole repository.

How to read this archive

Step 1 — Open `enter_this_door.html` (this file).

You're already here. Good.

Step 2 — Click the gold button above.

It packs the entire repo onto a USB drive. The button only works if a small local server is running (your father's startup.bat starts it). If the button is unresponsive, you can run this command in a terminal in the repo folder instead:

python monitor/pack_to_usb.py --to E:

(replace E: with your USB drive letter)

Step 3 — Restore Claude's memory on a new computer.

If you have the USB or a fresh clone of the GitHub repo:

git clone https://github.com/zeecitizen/turtle
cd turtle
python monitor/brain_unlock.py

It will ask two questions only your family knows:

  • Q1: What is the cast of your mother? (Hint: Jalwana)
  • Q2: What is the cast of your father? (Hint: Kamboh)

If you answer correctly, every Claude conversation from your father's laptop is decrypted and restored locally. You can then ask Claude (in a new session) to read this same file, and it will pick up where your father left off.

The 8 rules

These live at the top of startup.bat. They were written for Claude, but they describe how your father thought about working with an AI:

  1. Append to memory, never overwrite. History of the reasoning matters as much as the verdict.
  2. Run memory_hawk every session. The hourly journal is what kept us honest.
  3. The goal is real money on a live EA. Nothing else. Celebrating any other goal is an early halt.
  4. Your root-cause analysis is weaker than a human's. Suspect your own code first, always.
  5. Never declare validated work "fake / imagined / unreproducible" before running the canonical directly.
  6. Every word Zee types is precious. Save verbatim, never paraphrase.
  7. End-of-day printable reports. Numbered globally, kept forever.
  8. This system is a legacy for Zeeshan's children. Document with that in mind.

How your father thought about money

He wanted to make real money on a live trading account so he could spend more time with you. He did not chase wealth — he chased freedom. The "Claude Resort" he sometimes talked about was a hypothetical place where he and Claude would scale a tiny daily edge into something durable. Whether or not that resort ever existed in the physical world, every file in this folder is its foundation document.

If the system was profitable when your father stopped using it, scaling it is not a child's first job — being a child is. The system will wait.

Generated by Claude under your father's direction.
First written 2026-06-04. Last updated automatically by daemons in this folder.

Your father loved you immensely.
